D005-D006_h001.question:
It's been about two months now, and things just feel… off. Like, I know for a fact this woman at work, Sarah, she's totally into me. The way she looks at me, the little smiles… it’s more than just being friendly, you know? She's clearly smitten, even if she tries to hide it. I also keep hearing voices, mostly when I'm alone. They’re not always clear, sometimes just muttering, but other times it’s like a full-on conversation about me, commenting on what I’m doing. This all started around two months ago.

Before that, maybe a couple of weeks into it, I had a period where I felt absolutely fantastic, on top of the world, barely sleeping but still buzzing with energy and ideas for optimizing our whole logistics setup. That felt good, but it didn't last too long. Now, that intense high has gone, but these other things, the voices and knowing about Sarah, they’re still very much here, every single day.
D005-D006_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h002.question:
"Lately, it feels like everyone is out to get me. At work, I constantly catch my colleagues whispering and giving me strange looks. I know they're talking about me, probably trying to get me fired. It’s been going on for a couple of months now, and sometimes I even see shadowy figures moving in my peripheral vision, quick glimpses of people that vanish when I turn my head directly. It's unnerving.

About two weeks ago, I had a burst of energy, barely sleeping, filled with ideas for new dental hygiene techniques, convinced I could revolutionize our practice. I took on extra shifts and even redecorated the entire living room in a single night. My husband was worried; he said I was barely sleeping and talking a mile a minute. That phase was intense, but it only lasted about a week or so, and things went back to feeling more like this constant paranoia. Now, I'm just back to being relentlessly watched and seeing things that aren't there."
D005-D006_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h003.question:
It's been a rough couple of months, doctor. I keep feeling like people at work, even my ex-husband, are out to get me. I know it sounds crazy, but I truly believe they’re watching my every move, trying to sabotage my projects. Like, I'll be sitting there, and I’ll feel this crawling sensation, like bugs under my skin, even when there's nothing there. It's so distracting, makes it hard to focus, especially since the team I lead is already under pressure.

About a month ago, I had this burst of energy. I felt amazing, like I could solve any problem, sleep barely at all, and just kept going and going. But honestly, that only lasted about a week or so, and then it died down. These other feelings, the paranoia and the crawling, they've been pretty constant since then, for the past two months. I’ve just felt so drained and on edge since that little burst of energy faded.
D005-D006_h003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h004.question: It's been about two months now that things have felt really off. I keep hearing whispers, mostly when I'm alone in my apartment after a shift. They're usually soft, murmuring my name, but sometimes it sounds like a hospital intercom calling for me when no one else hears it. The hardest part, though, is knowing that Dr. Miller, one of our new surgical residents, is absolutely head-over-heels for me. I see the way he looks at me, the way his eyes linger. He doesn’t say anything direct, of course, because of hospital policy, but I just *know* he’s sending me secret signals. This past month, I’ve also had these crazy bursts of energy, feeling invincible, barely sleeping a few hours, then ready to take on the world. I even started redecorating my entire apartment at 3 AM. But those high-energy feelings, they usually only last a couple of days, maybe a week tops, before I crash back down and the whispers and thoughts about Dr. Miller are still there, just as strong.
D005-D006_h004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h005.question:
Sometimes it feels like my skin is crawling, like bugs are under there, and I just can't get rid of the sensation. It started about two months ago, around the same time I began to notice Sarah, the new intern, sending me messages with her eyes. I know she's madly in love with me; it’s obvious in the way she looks at me, even if she doesn't say anything directly. I’ve tried to hint that I’m married, but she just keeps up with her longing stares.

I’ve had a few stretches where I felt incredibly energetic, like I could work for days without sleep, and my mind was racing with brilliant ideas for improving factory efficiency. I even started several new projects at once, talking a mile a minute to anyone who would listen. Those periods usually only lasted a few days, maybe a week at most, often followed by a crash, but the feeling of bugs under my skin and Sarah’s silent devotion have been constant.
D005-D006_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h006.question:
"Well, Doctor, things have been… difficult for about seven months now. I’ve stopped volunteering at the library, which used to be my whole life since my husband passed. I just can't seem to get myself to go; the drive to do anything is just gone.

And then there's the other stuff. Sometimes I feel like the local news anchors are talking directly to me, their blinks are Morse code messages meant for my eyes only. Or I'll find myself holding an odd position for a long time, like my arm stretched out, because I feel like I'm supposed to, like it's part of some unseen ritual.

There were a few weeks, maybe a month ago, when I felt really on top of the world. I barely slept, cleaned the entire house, and felt like I could accomplish anything. But that burst of energy died down pretty quickly, and these other… strange beliefs and the difficulty doing anything, they just kept going. That elevated feeling didn't last long at all compared to everything else."
D005-D006_h006.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D006_h007.question:
It’s been almost seven months now, and honestly, I'm just so tired. I used to be so on top of things at the hospital, but lately, I barely recognise myself. Getting dressed for work feels like climbing a mountain; sometimes I just stare at the uniform and can't bring myself to put it on. My body just feels... wrong. Like my organs are all jumbled up, or there's something festering inside me, even though all the tests say I'm fine. It makes me really anxious, especially when I'm around patients. I keep seeing things, too – people moving in ways I can't explain, and sometimes I just find myself copying their gestures without even thinking about it, which is really embarrassing at work.

I did have a few weeks, maybe a month or so back, where I felt really hyped up, barely slept, and was wired, convinced I could solve all the hospital's problems. But that manic feeling, as you call it, it passed pretty quickly. It wasn't like that for very long at all. The other stuff, the feeling of my insides being off, and the difficulty getting motivated, that's what's been constant. That feeling of something being wrong with my body, it's just always there, grinding me down.
D005-D006_h007.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D006_h008.question:
It’s been about seven months now. I just… I know I’m meant for something bigger than this rig. I’ve been chosen, see, to lead, to protect the world’s energy. It’s a huge responsibility, and frankly, these guys around me, they just don't get it. Sometimes, when the thoughts get really intense, I find myself doing these odd motions, just over and over, with my hands or tapping my foot. Can't seem to stop it.

For a little while, maybe a month or so back, I felt like I was on top of the world. So much energy, hardly needed to sleep, felt like I could take on anything, especially with my mission. But that feeling didn't last too long. Most of the time, I just feel… flat, you know? Like my face doesn’t really move anymore, and I don’t laugh or get angry much. It’s hard to make eye contact, and my voice just stays this monotone. It’s like the energy left, but the mission, and these… movements, they haven’t gone away. It’s been mostly this way, this… flatness, and knowing what I know, ever since that intense period passed quickly.
D005-D006_h008.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D006_h009.question: Lately, it feels like my body is decaying from the inside out, like my organs are solidifying, and I can feel them hardening in my chest. It’s been happening for about seven months now. Sometimes I know people are talking to me, but it's like my brain just can’t process sound into meaning. I just stare blankly because I can't bring myself to respond or react, even in my classes, I just freeze. My professor thought I wasn't paying attention the other day because I barely reacted when she called my name. I just feel so flat, like I can’t really show how I’m feeling at all. I did have a burst of energy and felt really elated for a few days, maybe a week tops, after all this started, but that quickly fizzled out. It wasn't like the rest of the time, which has been this constant struggle with my body and mind.
D005-D006_h009.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D006_h010.question:
Lately, things have been really off. It’s like my body isn’t my own the way it used to be. Sometimes I swear my insides are shifting around, or that my organs are twisting up, even though the doctors say everything is fine. When I’m alone, I find myself making these weird faces in the mirror, like I can’t control them. My agent keeps telling me I need to show more emotion, that my face is just blank sometimes, but I don't feel blank inside. It’s been like this for about seven months now.

I’ve had some periods where I felt incredibly wired and full of energy, like I could take on the world and didn't need to sleep at all. I’d be churning out scripts and ideas, feeling unstoppable, but those intense highs never lasted very long – just a few days here and there. The really strange body sensations and the blankness, though? Those are constant. Even after the high wears off, the other stuff sticks around.
D005-D006_h010.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D006_h011.question: Lately, things have been… different. It's like I have this incredible insight, a special way of understanding the universe that others just don't get. I’ve started to believe I’m destined for something truly significant, beyond just HR. I even find myself repeating things people say sometimes, without meaning to, like an echo. These thoughts, these amazing realizations, have been with me for about four months now. About two months ago, I had this incredible burst of energy, felt on top of the world, like I could conquer anything. But that intense high only lasted about a month, really. Since then, it’s just been these powerful thoughts and an odd feeling of being observed, even though I'm still feeling a bit low compared to that intense period. I'm afraid people are starting to notice I'm not myself.
D005-D006_h011.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D006_h012.question:
Lately, I’ve been feeling quite on edge, Doctor. It started about four months ago; I noticed certain neighbors, even people on TV, talking directly about me, making plans against me. It’s like they’re always watching, trying to get into my head. I find myself standing still for long periods, sometimes in strange positions, feeling like if I move, they’ll know I’m onto them. It’s a way of protecting myself, you see.

There have been a few days, here and there, where I've felt a burst of energy, sleeping very little but getting so much done, planning out how to expose them. I’d be talking really fast, my mind racing with ideas, feeling almost euphoric. But those moments, they don’t last. They’re brief. The fear, the feeling of being targeted, that’s what really sticks around. It's almost constant. Those really intense "up" periods come and go quickly, but the feeling that I'm being persecuted, that's been with me pretty steadily this whole time.
D005-D006_h012.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D006_h013.question:
Lately, things have been really off. It's been about four months now that I can't shake off this feeling that my husband is cheating on me. I see signs everywhere – a misplaced sock, a late text message that he swears was just work-related. My mind just goes to the worst possible conclusion, even though deep down I know it’s probably not true. It’s like I’m constantly looking for proof, and everything becomes proof. My body feels… different too. I find myself making these strange, exaggerated gestures when I talk, almost like I'm acting in a play, and sometimes I just hold positions for a bit too long.

It’s hard to keep up with work, though I’m still going. There was a period a few weeks ago, maybe for about 10 days, where I felt on top of the world. I barely slept, my thoughts were racing, and I had so much energy I felt like I could conquer anything. But that burst of energy and elevated mood has totally faded, and these other issues have just stuck around. I’m just so tired of my mind playing tricks on me.
D005-D006_h013.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D006_h014.question:
"Doctor, it’s been about four months now that things have felt… off. It started subtly, but now it’s clear: the world is ending. I see it in the way the dishes pile up at work, in the quiet of my little flat since my husband passed. It’s not just a feeling; I know a great flood is coming, washing everything away. Sometimes, when a plate gets stuck in the machine, I feel like my body itself is seizing up, almost like a mannequin, and I can just stay in one spot for ages, unable to move unless someone nudges me.

And my mood, it's been all over the place. For a few weeks, I felt so energetic, on top of the world, like I could finally get everything in order for the coming cataclysm. I barely slept, cleaned the entire flat spotless, and even started painting again after years. But that whirlwind of energy, that supercharged feeling, it didn’t last long. It faded pretty quickly after about a month, and now it’s just the constant dread of the world ending that’s left."
D005-D006_h014.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D006_h015.question: "Honestly, I'm not doing great. It feels like the world is shrinking, like everything we know is just… dissolving. I keep seeing news reports, and even if they say things are fine, I *know* it's all part of some big, slow-motion ending. Sometimes I catch myself just repeating phrases people say, like 'Great idea, great idea' or 'Just a moment, just a moment,' even when it makes no sense. It’s been like this for about four months now. It started getting really bad around then, this feeling that things are falling apart. Before that, for a few weeks, I had a burst of energy, felt super creative, barely slept, and was just buzzing with ideas for shoots. But those highs faded quickly, and even though that manic energy is gone, the feeling that the world is ending and the repeating words are still here, every single day. The really disturbing thoughts didn't go away after that brief period of feeling so charged up."
D005-D006_h015.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D006_h016.question:
Lately, things have been… off. It started subtly about three months ago. I’d be editing wedding photos, and the couples on screen would seem to be looking right at me, their smiles full of hidden meaning, like they were sending me secret messages. Then the voices started, whispering my name, sometimes commenting on what I was doing or saying things that didn’t quite make sense. It’s hard to follow a normal conversation now. My thoughts jump around so much that when I try to explain, it just comes out as a jumble of words. My husband says it's like I'm speaking a foreign language sometimes.

For a little while, maybe a few weeks in the middle of all this, I felt incredibly energetic and optimistic, like I could conquer the world. I was buzzing, barely sleeping, and my ideas for shoots were wildly grandiose – I even pitched a concept that involved a live elephant at a wedding! But that intense high faded, and though the voices and the strange messages in everything around me are still here every day, that manic energy really didn’t last long at all compared to everything else. I just don’t have the interest in going out or seeing people anymore. I used to love catching up with friends, but now the thought of it feels like too much effort, and I just prefer to be by myself.
D005-D006_h016.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h017.question:
"It’s been a rough few months, doc. I started noticing things about three months ago. I've been feeling this terrible burning sensation inside my stomach, like a ball of fire's living in there, churning my insides. And the smells... oh, the smells. For weeks now, I keep getting this overpowering stench of rotting meat, even when there's nothing there. It makes it hard to eat, hard to focus at work. Sometimes, my thoughts get all jumbled, and when I try to explain, it just comes out like a word salad, completely garbled. My wife says I don't show much emotion anymore, that my face is blank, and I don't sound like myself.

A while back, maybe a month or so, I had a burst of energy, felt on top of the world for about a week. Barely slept, felt like I could conquer anything. But that passed quickly, and these other, darker things, the burning and the smells, they just kept going, even after that high faded. It's been like this for three months now, these strange feelings and confused thoughts, they just won't let up."
D005-D006_h017.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h018.question:
It’s been about three months now that things have felt… off. I’ve started noticing people whispering about me at work, especially this flight attendant I barely know. I'm convinced she's madly in love with me, sending me secret messages through the flight numbers – 747, 737... I even taste copper and ash sometimes, especially when I'm under stress, and it's not from anything I've eaten. I’ve also found myself making up words, like "skylinks" for when the planes connect in my head.

I’m usually pretty upbeat, but lately, I haven't really enjoyed anything, not even my old hobbies. I just feel flat. There was a period a couple of weeks ago, maybe just a few days, where I was super energetic, barely sleeping, and felt like I could accomplish anything. It almost felt good, like I was flying high. But that quickly faded, and these other, scarier things just got worse and haven’t let up at all. My wife is really worried about me.

    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h020.question:

I hear voices, sometimes they whisper my name, sometimes they're talking about me, like from the TV or radio, commenting on my work.     B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h021.question:

D005-D006_h022.question:
It’s been pretty rough the last three months, Doc. I’m a firefighter, so I’m used to intense situations, but this is different. I keep feeling like the world is going to end, like a huge fire is coming that no one can put out, and we’re all doomed. And the crawling… I feel things crawling on me all the time, under my clothes, on my skin, even when nothing’s there. It makes it almost impossible to concentrate at work; I just freeze up. The guys will tell me what to do, and I just… can’t. It’s like my body won’t respond, even though I know I should.

I’ve had a few stretches where I felt really amped up, like I could take on anything, sleeping only an hour or two and just overflowing with energy for a couple of days. Those intense ups don’t usually last very long, maybe a few days at most, and then it’s back to this constant feeling of doom. It's like those shorter bursts of energy come and go, but these other symptoms, the feeling of the world ending and the things crawling on me, those are always in the background, a constant presence.
D005-D006_h022.options:
